body.p: The first non-final Office action on the merits dated October 31, 2024, and the references cited therein have been carefully reviewed. Favorable reconsideration of this application in view of the following remarks and amendments is respectfully requested.
Claims 10, 14, and 18 are amended.
Claims 1-18 are currently pending for further examination and consideration.
A telephonic interview was conducted on January 16, 2025, between Primary

Examiner Bonnette and Applicant's representative, Amir Behnia (Reg. No. 50,215). TheInterview Summary Record (PTOL-413) correctly identifies all the participants, the date of the interview, the issues that were discussed, and accurately reflects a detailed description of the substance of the interview.
As a result of the Office action, claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being indefinite, as set forth on page 2 of the Office action.
Moreover, the following obviousness rejections under Section 103 are raised against the pending claims 1-18, as set forth on pages 3-14 of the Office action:
8. Claim(s) 1-4, 6, 7, 9-14, & 16-18 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being
unpatentable over French (Pub No. US 2013/0119202 A1) in view of Beck (Pub No. US
10. Claim(s) 5 & 15 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over French
(Pub No. US 2013/0119202 Al) in view of Beck (Pub No. US 2012/0043425 Al) as applied to
claims 1 & 14 above, and further in view of French (Pub No. US 2012/0025026 Al).
12. Claim(s) 8 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over French (Pub No. US 2013/0119202 Al) in view of Beck (Pub No. US 2012/0043425 Al) as applied to claim 1
above, and further in view of Tichborne et al. (Pub No. US 2014/0238501 A1).

These rejections are respectfully traversed in view of the foregoing amendments and for at least the following reasons, and favorable reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims are therefore respectfully requested.

The indefiniteness rejection of claim 10 is respectfully traversed. Claim 10 has been amended to correct the typographical error and it is now dependent from claim 9. Therefore, the indefiniteness rejection of claim 10 is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

The obviousness rejection of claim 1 is respectfully traversed. Applicant respectfully submits that neither French '202 nor Beck, taken individually or in combination thereof, teaches or discloses "wherein the inlet of the vapour recovery system is coupled to the opening without plugging it in to the opening." As discussed during the interview, French '202 is directed toward controlling refueling operations and monitoring tank pressure during refueling. Beck is directed toward refueling equipment connections. It is respectfully submitted that neither reference teaches or suggests a vapor recovery system that captures and stores fuel vapor during normal operation. Applicant submits that there is not a single disclosure of the term "vapor" in either reference. Moreover, neither reference teaches a "vapor recovery system", and French '202 simply shows a ground equipment 200 which is a fuel truck:
Therefore, as discussed and agreed during the interview, and as indicated in the
body.h1: Interview Summary, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is patentable over the prior
body.p: art combination, and the Section 103 obviousness rejection of claim 1 is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.
Moreover, as also discussed and agreed during the interview, claims 14 and 18 are

amended to recite the "without plugging it in to the opening" feature similar to claim 1 and, therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the obviousness rejections of claims 14 and 18 be withdrawn.

Claims 2-13 depend from claim 1, recite additional features and distinguish over the applied references for at least the reasons set forth above with respect to claim 1 and/or for the additional features recited.

Claims 15-17 depend from claim 14, recite additional features and distinguish over the applied references for at least the reasons set forth above with respect to claim 14 and/or for the additional features recited.
The Applicant has made a diligent effort to place the claims in condition for
allowance, and respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance, and an early notice to that effect is earnestly solicited.
If any issues remain that can be clarified by telephonic interview to advance

prosecution, Primary Examiner Bonnette is cordially invited to contact the Applicant's representative, Amir Behnia (Reg. No. 50,215) at (703) 816-4072 to arrange an interview.Also, the Applicant's representative can be contacted via email at abehnia@nixonvan.com noting that an Ecomm Authorization has been filed in this case allowing for email communications.
